text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER: High tail latency & queue buildup for tenant 'quantumcare' on dedicated-eu-west-1 pool. Error rate spike ~6% and p95 latency ~880ms. Auto-escalating to on-call.
oncall-maya: ack. Paging @sre-jordan and @runtime-luis. Good morning — I'm taking this one. What's the customer impact? can cs confirm?
cs-amy: QuantumCare on-call reported chat assistants timing out for a subset of sessions. Customer sees many "request timed out" errors during longer prompts. They're on dedicated pool (VPC) and have heavy concurrent long-context workloads.
sre-jordan: seeing a big backlog in tenant queue. `redis:tenant:quantumcare:pending` ~2400 entries, normally <200. Per-pod CPU not saturated but average batch size jumped a lot. Looks like a small number of very long requests are preventing batches from flushing.
runtime-luis: confirming. Scheduler logs show large batches stalling because of massive `max_batch_tokens` usage from their model profile. Current tenant config: `max_batch_tokens: 8192`, `max_batch_size: 64`. That lets long requests combine and push tail latency.
oncall-maya: immediate mitigation plan: (1) apply temporary tenant-level scheduler override to favor latency (lower max_batch_tokens & max_batch_size), (2) enable aggressive queue smoothing/shaper for tenant, (3) if needed, add a short-lived rate limit on their tenant burst. Any objections?
eng-ryan: +1 for latency-first for now. We should preserve logs to revert. Also note possible cost increase if we spin more smaller batches.
runtime-luis: I'll push a tenant override now. Endpoint: `POST https://admin.internal/api/tenants/quantumcare/scheduler-config` body below. Applying `max_batch_tokens: 512`, `max_batch_size: 8`, `min_batch_tokens: 32`, `queue_smoothing_alpha: 0.7`, `max_concurrent_batches: 6`, `tenant_shaper_weight: 1.0`.
runtime-luis: ```bash
curl -s -X POST \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"override": {"max_batch_tokens":512,"max_batch_size":8,"min_batch_tokens":32,"queue_smoothing_alpha":0.7,"max_concurrent_batches":6,"tenant_shaper_weight":1.0}, "ttl_seconds": 1800}' \
  https://admin.internal/api/tenants/quantumcare/scheduler-config
```
runtime-luis: applied. API returned `200 OK` and `override_id: ovr-7a3b`. Rolling out to all replicas in eu-west-1 now.
oncall-maya: monitoring. Can someone tail the per-tenant queue metric and p95 latency? `grafana -> tenant.quantumcare.*`
sre-jordan: watching: queue depth falling from 2400 -> 450 in ~45s. p95 latency dropped from 880ms -> 210ms after override. Error rate down to 1.2%.
cs-amy: reported back to customer: they see immediate improvement in tests. They're still running a large batch of sessions; will monitor for the next 30m.
eng-ryan: good. Note: we changed `max_concurrent_batches` up to 6 which can increase GPU context switches — watch per-pod CPU/GPU utilization.
ops-jen: I'm going to temporarily enable tenant-level burst limiter at 20 rps if we see another spike. Will wait 10m to confirm.
runtime-luis: collecting logs for postmortem: scheduler trace + batch compositions. Saved as `s3://redwood-ops/incident/quantumcare/1862349999/`.
oncall-maya: quick risk note: this override will reduce throughput and increase per-token cost. We need CS approval before leaving in place. CS, can you coordinate with customer for a controlled rollout of prompt/usage limits?
cs-amy: pinged customer PM. They've agreed to keep override for 20 minutes while they run acceptance tests, then we'll discuss a long-term plan (model quantization, prompt truncation, or staged batch policy).
sre-jordan: created a short-lived canary: `kubectl get pods -l tenant=quantumcare -o wide` to ensure pods didn't crash during config push — all pods green.
runtime-luis: FYI there's an open runtime ticket to add a new knob `max_batch_token_window` to prevent a single request from monopolizing a batch. Filed as RUNTIME-3421.
oncall-maya: if things stay stable for next 25m we'll start rolling back TTL->0 at 30m and replace with a gradual config: `max_batch_tokens: 1024`, `max_batch_size: 16`, `queue_smoothing_alpha: 0.5`.
eng-ryan: taking note for perf docs: add a recipe for "latency-first tenant override" showing these exact values and tradeoffs.
ops-jen: alerting thresholds adjusted for tenant: p95>500ms -> page; p95>300ms -> notify #eng-runtime. Lowered temporarily.
cs-amy: customer confirms acceptance tests passed at +12m. They're happy with latency improvement.
oncall-maya: handoff: I'm on-call for another 15m then handing to @sre-jordan. Action items for handoff:
- Leave current override until 30m mark (ttl reminder set)
- If stable, move to gradual config (1024/16/0.5)
- If queue rebuilds, re-enable burst limiter and escalate to infra
- Attach logs to INC-quantumcare-1862349999
sre-jordan: taking on after 15m. I'll monitor and escalate if any regressions. Thanks all.
oncall-maya: closing loop: incident-bot, please annotate incident as "mitigated - tenant override applied; p95 improved; monitoring" and set reminder for config rollback at +30m. :white_check_mark:
incident-bot: Noted. Incident annotated. Reminder set for 30 minutes. :ok_hand:
oncall-maya: final: brief retrospective notes — root cause: tenant workload includes occasional very long prompts that allowed single-request batches to balloon `max_batch_tokens`. Long-term fixes: tenant guidance (truncate/stream prompts), fallback model variant with lower context, runtime feature RUNTIME-3421, and optional tenant QoS/burst budgeting.
cs-amy: filing a customer-facing summary and follow-up meeting invite.
sre-jordan: I'll own postmortem; adding timeline and graphs to `postmortems/quantumcare-1862349999.md`.
eng-ryan: thx team. :thumbsup:"
